title: Implement request-flattening and tenant-grade soft-circuit for Hosted API 5xx surges
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: Implement a request-flattening layer at the edge and a per-tenant soft-circuit mechanism in the request admission controller to reduce 5xx waves caused by retry amplification and fan-out during customer escalations. Goal is to reduce customer-visible 5xx rate by deduplicating identical inflight requests, limiting proxy fan-out, and progressively degrading tenants before full eviction.
background: Over the last three months we've observed several customer escalations where client-side retries and orchestrated uploads caused a multiplication of identical requests to our serving runtime. The amplification pattern is: client retry -> edge replays / fanout to multiple model variants -> runtime queue saturation -> KV cache churn -> 5xx/timeouts. Existing mitigations (connection backoff, generic circuit breakers) reduced impact but were either too aggressive or too late in the pipeline. We need a lightweight, deployable mitigation that: 1) coalesces identical inflight requests, 2) enforces per-tenant admission windows (soft-circuit scores) and 3) applies transparent graceful degradation (e.g., route to cached prefix or lower-compute variant) before hard-eviction.
scope: In scope: edge request fingerprinting/dedupe, in-memory inflight coalescer per edge instance, tenant soft-circuit scoring and admission thresholds, API to declare degradable model variants, tracing/metrics for dedupe-hit-rate and soft-circuit decisions, runbook updates and canary rollout. Out of scope: persistent global dedupe store, long-term billing model changes, deep kernel/runtime rearchitecture.
design_decisions: 1) Use a per-edge in-memory coalescer keyed by request fingerprint (model+input-hash+tenant+route) with an optional short TTL (250ms default) to coalesce rapid duplicate requests. 2) Soft-circuit is a scoring function combining recent 5xx rate, queue latency, and dedupe hit ratio — thresholds configurably tiered by customer SLA. 3) Degradation actions are ordered: a) return cached prefix if available, b) downgrade to a compatible lower-cost variant, c) respond with a synthetic partial response (e.g., short summary) before hard-eviction. 4) Keep fingerprinting deterministic and composable with existing idempotency tokens. 5) All decisions must emit structured events for Console visualization.
acceptance_criteria:
- End-to-end integration tests that validate coalescing: when three identical requests arrive within 250ms only one backend request is performed.
- In production canary, 40% reduction in tenant-originated 5xxs for synthetic surge tests.
- New metrics visible in Console: dedupe_requests_total, dedupe_hit_ratio, tenant_soft_circuit_score, tenant_degrade_actions_total.
- Runbook updated and Customer Success notified with mitigation steps.
- PR accepted and deployed to canary regions without regression in latency p50/p95 outside tolerance.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge coalescer + metrics behind feature flag. 2) Canary deploy to region-us-east-2 for 72h with synthetic surge harness (see Automation doc). 3) Enable per-tenant soft-circuit with conservative thresholds for 5 customers on canary. 4) Monitor dedupe hit ratio and SLOs; iterate thresholds. 5) Gradually promote to 50% edges, then global. 6) Once stable, bake into runtime-1.24 release.
monitoring_and_alerts: Add Prometheus metrics and Console dashboards: dedupe_hit_ratio (alert if < 0.5 during surge), inflight_coalescer_size (alert if > threshold), tenant_soft_circuit_score (alert if > high_score), degrade_action_rate (alert if spree of degradations). Create an incident runbook entry 'IF dedupe_hit_ratio drops OR degrade_action_rate spikes -> scale edge to handle more inflight capacity and consider increasing dedupe-window temporarily.'
security_and_compliance_notes: Fingerprinting must avoid storing PII. The request fingerprint will be computed from a salted hash of model identifier + truncated input hash + tenant id. Configurable salt stored in KMS. Documented in confluence and flagged for security review if fingerprinting expands to persistent stores (out of scope now).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: coalescer TTL too long may increase tail latency for unique requests — mitigate by conservative default (250ms) and pilot. Risk: incorrect fingerprint collisions -> wrong response served to another tenant (avoid by including tenant id in key and using crossover checks). Risk: tenants with strict SLAs may not accept silent degradation — provide per-tenant opt-out and audit logs.
